newsitem.title: UK: BSkyB shares hit by gloomy WSJ report.
newsitem.headline: BSkyB shares hit by gloomy WSJ report.

text.p: Shares in satellite broadcaster British Sky Broadcasting Group came under pressure on Thursday from a report in the Wall Street Journal Europe detailing the rise of competitive pressure in the British market.

BSkyB shares, which have risen as high as 698p this year, traded at 518p by 1006 GMT, down four pence or 0.76 percent on the day. The market was down 0.2 percent. Some 760,000 BSkyB shares had changed hands by that time.
"There's nothing particularly new in the report but it does a good job of highlighting Sky's position and some people have got a bit nervous about it," one market maker said.
The report said rising interest and investment in digital broadcasting technology were threatening BSkyB "with the kind of competitive pressure it has never really faced."
"For analog-laden BSkyB, getting started with digital technology is going to drain resources," the report said, adding that BSkyB would face more competition for original programming.

Dealers said comments from television industry watchdog Don Cruickshank on Wednesday evening indicated BSkyB could be in for a tougher time. Cruickshank told a news conference that Britain would only license access technology for digital television on "fair, reasonable and non-discriminatory" terms.

Cruickshank said he would prevent the first market entrant into digital television from exploiting a monopoly position. BSkyB is planning to launch digital satellite television in late 1997 and will be the first player in the British market.
